constraints: Use the existing canonical SystemBuilderRevision, AssetComposition, AssetInstance, AssetPlacement, AssetBinding, exact definitions, and application validators; drag state is transient UI state only.
The visual canvas must represent predefined named slots and semantic ordering rather than arbitrary coordinates, user-authored dimensions, or renderer-only layout metadata.
Every pointer or touch drop must resolve to the same pure bounded add, reorder, reparent, wrap, or layout-remap operation used by the complete keyboard and button path.

The center canvas may render only registered side-effect-free Foundation surfaces and safe fixtures; it must never execute unqualified backing resources, imported code, backend logic, or deployment behavior.
Desktop and thin client must consume one shared editor shell and one platform client contract with exact workspace context, optimistic save conflicts, and no host-specific composition policy.
The wide mockup layout should keep palette, canvas, properties, and layers visible; narrower layouts must use accessible drawers or panel tabs without losing function, focus order, or source order.
Selection, focus, hover, drag overlay, zoom, panel size, and open-panel state are presentation state and must not enter immutable system revisions.
A layout change for an existing system must be explicit, previewable, cancelable, and deterministic, preserving compatible content and exposing unmatched content rather than silently deleting it.
Any new drag-and-drop dependency must be version-pinned, license/security reviewed, isolated behind shared UI interaction adapters, and verified in desktop packaging and thin-client builds.
Keep the old slot-composer roadmap stopped after its verified Increment 3; do not resume its unstarted Increment 4 in parallel with this replacement roadmap.

discovery.summary: The completed slot-composer foundations already provide exact workspace asset discovery, required system roots, predefined application/page layouts, canonical named slots and placements, pure add/reorder/reparent/wrap/remove draft operations, protected nodes, bounded undo/redo, schema-generated configuration, typed connections, a keyboard tree, safe recursive preview, and desktop/thin-client parity. The current UI does not yet match the supplied visual-composer mockup: creation controls and layout choices sit above the editor, the asset/canvas/tree workspace exists only in Structure mode, configuration and connections replace the whole workspace, the center is a semantic hierarchy rather than a safe editable visual rendering, and no pointer/touch drag interaction exists. The mockup can therefore be implemented as a shared interaction and presentation layer over the existing canonical draft, with one application-owned layout-remapping seam where changing an existing layout requires deterministic placement mapping. No new persistence graph or renderer-owned system truth is needed.

acceptanceCriteria.description: For an open system, wide screens present the asset/layout palette, primary editable canvas, properties inspector, and Layers and Structure tree simultaneously beneath one coherent editor toolbar; selected system, revision, dirty, validation, loading, error, conflict, and save states remain understandable without switching between disconnected forms.

A compatible asset can be inserted from the palette, reordered within a slot, or moved across compatible slots using pointer, touch, keyboard pickup/move/drop, or explicit controls; every successful interaction calls the same bounded canonical command, every invalid target explains why it is unavailable, cancellation changes nothing, and no drag-library state enters a revision or transport payload.

The canvas recursively renders the current unsaved named-slot hierarchy with registered side-effect-free Foundation renderers, visible selection and slot overlays, bounded desktop/tablet/mobile frames, and truthful unsupported/nonvisual states while never executing unqualified backing resources, imported code, backend logic, network calls, builds, or deployments.

Predefined layout choices can create a system or initiate an explicit reviewed layout change; deterministic mapping preserves compatible instances, configuration, bindings, and semantic order, exposes unmatched content in an Unassigned region, supports cancel/undo/redo/stale conflict, and saves only as a new immutable revision without rewriting its source.

Selecting an asset from the canvas or Layers and Structure tree updates both surfaces and the persistent properties inspector; schema-backed Design, Data, and Events sections edit only supported configuration and declared endpoints, tree keyboard behavior follows expected expansion/navigation conventions, and containment remains separate from typed connections.

The shared workspace retains every editor function through accessible panels or drawers at medium and narrow widths, avoids unintended page-level two-dimensional scrolling, preserves logical source and focus order, restores focus after drawers/dialogs/drags, provides tailored instructions and live announcements, honors reduced motion, and keeps explicit native-control alternatives discoverable.

Desktop and thin client use the same shared visual editor and canonical client operations for create/open, Manage handoff, edit, undo/redo, validate, save, reopen, preview, and Build and Test entry; focused tests and host builds prove no renderer-local persistence, workspace fallback, host-specific composition rule, or transport divergence.

risks: Nested slot collision cannot be delegated to generic closest-center sorting because compatibility, cardinality, protected roots, cycles, unassigned content, and canonical order are application constraints.

JSDOM does not provide production layout geometry; collision and command resolution need pure model tests, while focused component tests should cover sensor wiring, keyboard behavior, announcements, and cancellation without pretending to be full browser qualification.
Making safe preview nodes selectable or droppable must not allow definition-provided components, raw backing-resource markup, or backend logic to enter the React tree.

A four-region wide editor can become unusable under zoom; side panels must become accessible drawers or tabs before widths force clipped controls, while the canvas alone may use a bounded manipulation viewport.
Layout switching is a canonical data transformation, not presentation state; renderer-only mapping would risk silent deletion and cross-host drift.
Drag activation on whole cards can steal clicks and scrolling; dedicated handles, activation constraints, explicit controls, reduced-motion behavior, and focus restoration are required.
The runtime dependency change must pass production and development advisory checks, license review, thin-client bundling, and Electron packaging before Increment 1 can complete.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A packaged Windows desktop application and supported thin-client browser each complete create, choose or change layout, drag assets into and across slots, reorder, configure Design/Data/Events, connect declared ports, undo/redo, preview, save, reopen, enter from Manage, and reach Build and Test using their real IPC/API paths without console, transport, or renderer errors.

Mouse, touch-equivalent pointer, and keyboard users can perform equivalent structural operations; screen-reader semantics and announcements identify source, valid destination, result, and cancellation; toolbar/tree/dialog/panel behavior follows documented keyboard conventions; and visible focus is never lost after panel changes, drops, errors, or dialogs.

At supported wide, medium, narrow, 320-CSS-pixel-equivalent zoom, reduced-motion, high-contrast, light, and dark configurations, every function remains available, non-canvas content avoids unintended two-dimensional scrolling, semantic source order remains correct, and reviewed baselines show no overlapping, clipped, hidden, or unreachable controls.

Malformed drag identifiers, invented slots, incompatible/revoked assets, oversized hierarchies/configuration, unsafe renderer inputs, and unqualified implementation resources fail closed with bounded redacted messages and never cause code execution, filesystem/network access, cross-workspace reads, build/release/deployment actions, or persisted partial mutations.

Representative compositions at documented node/depth/slot bounds meet recorded interaction and rendering targets; interrupted or canceled drags, failed layout changes, renderer exceptions, stale/conflicting saves, reloads, and rollback recover to a coherent canonical draft without immutable revision loss or duplicated placement state.

Dependency review, architecture and context documentation, keyboard/help guidance, support limits, rollback, exclusions, and qualification evidence match implemented behavior, and all applicable repository checks, builds, Windows packaging, and the final full suite pass with zero failures.

plan.summary: Qualify the visual composer with one deterministic, resource-aware test seam rather than separate ad hoc scripts: add pinned test-only Playwright/axe tooling and isolated host launchers, strengthen deterministic bounds/recovery coverage, run the same role-driven workflow against packaged Electron IPC and a real thin-client API host one at a time, review accessible/responsive visual states, repair findings with focused regressions, then run the costly repository gates once.

risks: Packaged desktop first-run identity uses a native dialog; the harness must stub it through Playwright's documented Electron main-process evaluation and fail clearly if startup races.

E2E state and server processes must use isolated roots, fixed bounded ports, one worker, sanitized logs, and reliable teardown so qualification never touches contributor data or leaves background load.

Automated axe and accessibility-tree evidence cannot be presented as full WCAG, screen-reader-product, or manual security certification; claims must remain scoped to the exact Chromium/Electron environments exercised.
Timing on a shared workstation is observational controlled evidence, not a portable performance guarantee; hard deterministic bounds stay in ordinary focused tests.
Visual snapshots can become brittle; limit them to representative composer regions and explicit wide, medium, narrow, forced-colors, reduced-motion, light, and dark scenarios.
research.summary: The repository already has canonical composition bounds, safe preview truncation, deterministic draft/application tests, Windows packaging, production builds, and a qualification policy, but it has no real browser/Electron E2E or automated accessibility harness. The smallest production qualification seam is test-only Playwright plus axe tooling: launch the packaged Electron executable against isolated user data, launch the thin client with a real isolated local server/API, drive the same role-based workflow with one worker, capture sanitized structured evidence and reviewed visual baselines, and add focused scale/recovery/security probes around existing bounds. Sidebar/panel/drag state remains transient and no test hook may widen production authority.

increments.rollback: Disable the visual editor route and restore the verified semantic editor entry while retaining all canonical slot-aware revisions as readable and editable through explicit controls. Remove the drag dependencies only after no visual-editor imports remain. Preserve diagnostic and qualification evidence; never flatten layouts, delete revisions, or weaken safe-rendering and workspace boundaries during rollback.
